common_name: Asheville After Dark Daylily (Award of Merit Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; registered by Paul Selman in 2014, it won the AHS Award of Merit in 2023 after an Honorable Mention in 2020.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun and divide crowded clumps every three to four years. Asheville After Dark, hybridized by Paul Selman from Unending Melody crossed with Bella Sera and registered in 2014, bears raspberry rose pink flowers with darker veins and a burgundy plum eye above a yellow-to-green throat, with a ruffled burgundy plum and white picotee edge, on dormant, tetraploid, 34-inch scapes that rebloom. It climbed the American Hemerocallis Society's Pyramid of Awards, earning an Honorable Mention in 2020 before winning the national Award of Merit in 2023.
